title: [B1 • Band 5.0] Bài 205: The Cognitive Horizons of Deep-Space Missions
passageHtml:
PASSAGE 205 (LEVEL B1 • BAND 5.0)

The Cognitive Horizons of Deep-Space Missions

Paragraph 1. As space agencies design rockets for future human trips to Mars, medical researchers are studying an equally difficult challenge: protecting the human mind during extreme isolation. A journey to Mars will force four to six astronauts to stay inside a small enclosed home, roughly the size of a shipping container, for nearly three years. On the International Space Station (ISS), astronauts can see Earth below and talk to flight controllers almost immediately. On a Mars mission, however, radio signals will suffer a communication delay of up to twenty-two minutes each way, making live conversation impossible.

Paragraph 2. To understand how long-term isolation affects human behaviour, scientists study extreme test stations on Earth. One leading example is Concordia Research Station, located on a freezing Antarctic plateau 3,200 metres above sea level. During the nine-month Antarctic winter, outdoor temperatures regularly fall below minus eighty degrees Celsius, and emergency evacuation is impossible. Inside the base, international crews live in an unchanging white world with zero natural sunlight for four straight months, recycled air, and no smells of plants or rain.

Paragraph 3. Careful brain checks at Concordia show clear signs of mental slowdown after three or four months. Regardless of personal toughness, crew members begin to forget details more easily, take twice as long to solve problems, and feel less emotional. Brainwave recordings reveal an unusual rise in slow theta waves, which normally appear during light sleep or quiet rest. Essentially, when nothing new happens around us, the brain lowers its active speed in order to save energy.

Paragraph 4. Team relationships also become delicate during long missions. In the first weeks, crews feel united and positive, but minor disagreements over habits, food, and daily chores slowly grow. Psychologist Dr. Alistair Finch explains that astronauts often use a mental habit called 'displacement'. Instead of arguing with fellow astronauts right beside them—which could hurt teamwork—they push their anger toward mission managers back on Earth. Although this keeps peace inside the cabin, crews may start ignoring important navigation instructions from ground control.

Paragraph 5. To protect astronaut mental health, engineers are developing smart support tools. Simple entertainment like watching films fails to reverse sensory boredom. Instead, NASA researchers are testing interactive virtual reality (VR) systems filled with mountain forests, ocean waves, and gentle breezes, which temporarily refresh memory performance. Additionally, engineers are building AI computer helpers inside spacecraft systems. By checking small shifts in a crew member's voice, facial expressions, and typing speed, the software can notice early sadness days before the astronaut feels it, quietly adjusting cabin lighting or daily tasks.

groups.title: Questions 6–10
groups.instructions: Do the following statements agree with the information in the passage? Write TRUE, FALSE, or NOT GIVEN.

steps: Đoạn 1: "...suffer a communication delay of up to twenty-two minutes..."
Đoạn 2: "...zero natural sunlight for four straight months..."
Đoạn 3: "...lowers its active speed in order to save energy."
Đoạn 4: "...ignoring important navigation instructions from ground control."

q6.text: Crews on the ISS experience the same 22-minute radio delay as future Mars astronauts.

steps: Đoạn 1: Phi hành gia trên ISS nói chuyện gần như tức thì (talk to flight controllers almost immediately).

q7.text: After three to four months, astronauts often take longer to solve problems.

steps: Đoạn 3: "...take twice as long to solve problems..."

q8.text: Displacement helps crew members avoid fighting directly with one another.

steps: Đoạn 4: Thay vì cãi nhau với đồng đội bên cạnh, họ trút bực dọc lên nhóm mặt đất để giữ hòa khí.

q9.text: Astronauts at Concordia Station grow fresh vegetables indoors during polar winter.

steps: Đoạn 2: Chỉ nói không có mùi cây cối (no smells of plants), không nhắc việc trồng rau trong nhà.

q10.text: AI computer tools can spot early stress before astronauts realise it themselves.

steps: Đoạn 5: "...notice early sadness days before the astronaut feels it..."
